newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-FAA order could affect freight cos.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-FAA order could affect freight cos.

text.p: -- Gruntal & Co said the Federal Aviation Administration may issue a so-called "airworthiness directive" shortly regarding certain Boeing Co 727 aircraft that have been converted into cargo freighters by after-market refurbishers.

-- said the airworthiness directive involves the structural integrity of about 320 older 727-model planes that have been converted into cargo service. The directive will not affect 727s that have been rebuilt by Boeing, Gruntal said.

-- said Federal Express Corp has about 120 of these aircraft in its fleet of about 550 planes. Emery Worldwide, a unit of Consolidated Freightways Inc, uses about 15-20 of those planes. Airborne Freight Corp will not likely be affected by the possible directive since it uses McDonnell Douglas Corp planes.
-- said the FAA is concerned that the 727s have structurally weak forward-section floor beams, possibly weak cargo doors, hinges and forward bulkhead barriers.
-- said it is likely the FAA will require structural and wiring improvements.
-- said until adjustments are made, weight permitted in the forward section of the 727s may be restricted.

-- said these possible actions could mean additional costs to carriers, travelers and shippers over the near-term. Long-term the possible directive would ensure steady passenger travel and air cargo growth.
-- Federal Express lost 5/8 to 52-1/2, Consolidated Freightways lost 1/4 to 28-1/2. Airborne Freight gained 1/8 to 33-1/8.
-- FAA representatives did not return calls seeking comment.
